subject: Post-call: QuoinHealth discovery + deployment outline
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Torres <atorres@quoinhealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 08 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: QuoinHealth discovery + deployment outline

Hi Alex — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our call so we have alignment before the technical deep-dive:

Key pain points you called out:
- Real-time triage assistant must respond within strict latency windows for clinician UX (p95 target ~120ms for short context flows).
- High concurrency during shift changes: spikes up to ~300 RPS for lightweight prompts, sustained baseline ~45 RPS across the region.
- Cost sensitivity for long-run batch processing (daily summarization jobs) — want to avoid overprovisioning GPU capacity.
- Data residency: PHI stays in their VPC; Redwood Private deployment is being considered.

Goals we agreed on:
1) Confirm feasibility for front-line assistant with p95 latency <= 150ms (goal 120ms) at 45 RPS baseline, 300 RPS bursts (with graceful degradation to smaller model variants).
2) Support for a verification pipeline: embeddings + rerank for record linking, and a separate async summarization job that can run on cheaper quantized weights.
3) Proof-of-concept on dedicated capacity in us-east with a canary route to Hosted for overflow/burst.

Technical summary / constraints you shared:
- Primary model family: decoder-only chat-optimized model, ~7B-13B parameter range (we recommended evaluating 7B quantized for latency and a 13B variant for quality fallback).
- Typical prompt size: 180-350 tokens; KV cache warm hits expected for multi-step dialog sessions.
- Expected average output length: 60 tokens for assistant responses; some long-form summaries (~3k tokens) will be async.

Suggested immediate next steps (action owners in parens):
- I’ll put together a topology sketch with latency/cost tradeoffs and an SLO matrix (Hannah).
- Jordan will run a quick capacity model for the 45 RPS baseline and 300 RPS burst (Jordan).
- Alex to introduce procurement and cloud/network ops for the Private deployment discussion (Alex).

Attachments: small topology sketch + blank SLO spreadsheet attached for your team to annotate.

If that matches your notes, I’ll schedule a technical deep-dive next week (30–45m) to walk the topology and perf targets with your infra team.

Thanks,
Hannah

Hannah — this is perfect, thanks for the thorough recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- The 300 RPS burst assumption is during two 10–15 minute windows per day (shift overlaps). Outside of those windows we expect the load to be closer to 35–50 RPS.
- For PHI handling we will require a VPC-hosted control plane and customer-managed KMS for keys; our security team will want the SOC2 artifact pack.
- The asynchronous long summaries can tolerate higher latency (minutes) so we’re open to running those on quantized variants or even CPU-based runners overnight.

I’ve looped in Priya (clinical informatics) and procurement — Priya will join the technical deep-dive. Procurement, please take a look at the blank SLO matrix and flag any procurement-specific SLAs (billing cadence, termination notice).

Alex
Alex Torres | Head of Clinical Platforms | QuoinHealth

Subject: Internal: QuoinHealth capacity sketch and perf assumptions

Hannah / Kim — quick internal note before the deep-dive so we go into the call with aligned numbers. I ran a lightweight capacity model based on Alex’s numbers and our runtime profiles (rough early estimates):

Assumptions:
- Baseline steady-state: 45 RPS, avg tokens in+out ~260 tokens total (prompt + response + metadata).
- Burst scenario: 300 RPS for 15 minutes; we’ll route overflow to Hosted with a lower-cost 7B quantized variant as fallback.
- P95 latency target: 150ms for the primary route; stretch goal 120ms for the 7B optimized path with 4–8 token batching.

Preliminary topology recommendation:
1) Private Dedicated Pool (us-east) with 2x NVidia A100-equivalent nodes reserved for baseline (handles ~60–80 RPS with optimized batching and KV cache).
2) Autoscaling + burst policy: add 4 burst nodes pre-warmed (fast spin-up) and allow overflow to Redwood Hosted API in the same region for brief bursts (with canary weighting to avoid noisy neighbor effects).
3) Model variants: primary 7B int8-perf compiled for low-latency; fallback 13B quantized for higher quality. Async summarization jobs run on a separate job queue using 13B int4-nightly capacity or CPU workers for cost savings.

Open questions for the deep-dive:
- Network egress limits and cross-VPC peering latency to your EHR — need procurement/cloud ops to confirm acceptable RTT.
- KMS/HSM integration details and whether we should submit a pre-signed MSP runbook for your security team.
- Clear definition of degraded behavior: which features can fall back to lower-quality model vs. queueing.

I’ll bring a simple cost vs latency chart and a short runbook for canary/fallback routing. Kim — can you validate our node sizing assumptions before the call?

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Blake | Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
